Definition: strengthened from a primary τρέω (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear:--be afraid, trembling.
BiblicalUsage: The healed woman came trembling, and the presumptuous do not tremble at all. The woman came trembling and falling down before Jesus and told Him why she had touched Him, and Peter says the presumptuous are not afraid to speak evil of dignities — they do not tremble where they should.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the woman who trembled shows the way: she came, she fell down, she was healed — and the men who will not tremble are condemned.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
